 Yakin to rotate as Akanji adds to Swiss absences 
 Image source, SNS Published 16 November 2026, 07:13 GMT 
 Internazionale defender Manuel Akanji has become Switzerland's fourth key absentee to face Scotland, but head coach Murat Yakin can see only "opportunities and possibilities" given his side have already won Nations League Group B1. 
 Scotland must win in St Gallen on Tuesday to have any chance of finishing runners-up and securing a promotion play-off place.
 The unbeaten Swiss were already without their top two midfielders - captain Granit Xhaka of Sunderland and Aston Villa's Johan Manzambi - as well as Nottingham Forest winger Dan Ndoye, before losing the former Manchester City 31-year-old to a muscle issue.
 Yakin pointed out that they were also without Xhaka and striker Breel Embolo for the 3-0 win over Scotland at Hampden last month and said: "We will make sure we get 11 good players on to the pitch.
 "It's good thing we have won the group already. It's now an opportunity to make changes.
 "We have enough opportunities and possibilities. We will rotate a bit, but we first have to make sure that we have a stable defence with experienced defenders."
 Yakin revealed that 20-year-old Sion striker Winsley Boteli will earn his fourth senior cap, while 23-year-old Young Boys midfielder Alvyn Sanches will be handed his seventh, both from the start.
 "It has been a fantastic year, a great year," the head coach added. "We reached all of our goals."
